entries.question: What tribe was Aijalon from?
entries.summary: Joshua 21:23-24 lists Aijalon as a Levitical city given out of the tribe of Dan, while 1 Chronicles 6:66, 69 lists Aijalon as a Levitical city given out of the tribe of Ephraim.
entries.commentary:
Two parallel Levitical-city lists, two different parent tribes for Aijalon. Joshua 21:23-24: "And out of the tribe of Dan... Aijalon with her suburbs, Gathrimmon with her suburbs." 1 Chronicles 6:66, 69: "The tribe of Ephraim... Aijalon with her suburbs, and Gathrimmon with her suburbs." The Chronicler is clearly working from a parallel source to Joshua 21 — the city pairings, the formula, even the suburb-language are nearly identical — but the parent tribe attribution differs.

The apologetic harmonization runs the historical-shift reading. Sara Japhet and Roddy Braun in their Chronicles commentaries argue that Aijalon was originally Danite (matching Joshua 21) but later transferred to Ephraim's territorial control after the Danite migration north (Judges 18). Since Dan effectively abandoned its southern territory, Ephraim absorbed the surrounding cities, and the Chronicler — writing centuries later — accurately reflects the post-Danite-migration administrative reality. So both texts can be true, just at different historical moments.

The migration-shift read has actual textual support. Judges 18 does narrate Dan's mass migration north, and the southern Danite cities did revert to neighboring tribes. 1 Chronicles 7:24 places Ephraim's territory in the area surrounding Aijalon. The Chronicler is well-known for updating geographical and administrative information from his sources to reflect later realities. So the reading isn't ad hoc.

Where it gets shakier is the textual-criticism dimension. The tribal lists in Joshua 21 and 1 Chronicles 6 are widely understood as variants of a single underlying source document. Sara Japhet's *I & II Chronicles* commentary in OTL and the textual notes in Steven McKenzie's commentary both observe that the two lists also disagree on the parent tribe of Gath-rimmon — Joshua 21:25 has it from the half-tribe of Manasseh while 1 Chron 6:69 (and apparently also the same context as Aijalon) has it from Ephraim. Plus the LXX of Joshua 21:24 has variants. So this isn't a clean "Joshua reflects period A, Chronicles reflects period B" sequence — it's two textually unstable lists with the kind of low-level corruption that scribal transmission of city-lists typically produces.

The critical-scholarly read combines both: the Levitical-city lists reflect an ideal program rather than continuously functioning administrative reality (Albrecht Alt, John Spencer), and the textual variants between Joshua 21 and 1 Chronicles 6 are partly real history (Dan's migration, Ephraim's expansion) and partly transmission errors. The contradiction is a real textual one even if the underlying administrative reality may have shifted; the historical-shift defense works in part but doesn't rescue the lists from being divergent witnesses to a fluid tradition.

answers.answer_explanation:
And out of the tribe of Dan ... Aijalon with her
				          suburbs, Gathrimmon with her suburbs. Joshua 21:23-24

The tribe of Ephraim ... Aijalon with her suburbs, and
				          Gathrimmon with her suburbs. 1 Chronicles 6:66, 69

assessment.variant_description: Joshua 21 and 1 Chronicles 6 are variant copies of a single Levitical-city source; they disagree on Aijalon's parent tribe (Dan vs Ephraim) and likewise on Gath-rimmon (Manasseh vs Ephraim), and the LXX of Joshua 21:24 preserves further variation, indicating textual instability in the city-lists.
assessment.critical_apparatus_ref: BHS apparatus at Joshua 21:23-24; cf. Japhet, I & II Chronicles (OTL), on the parallel Levitical-city lists
assessment.reasoning: No prior assessment supplied; the divergence is plausibly part historical (Dan's migration/Ephraim's expansion) and part scribal corruption in textually unstable parallel city-lists, with scholars genuinely divided between the historical-shift and transmission-error explanations, so disputed is the safest grade and a real textual dimension is flagged.

issues.problem: The variant_description and apparatus citation lean on a specific 'LXX of Joshua 21:24' variation bearing on Aijalon, and assert textual instability as the basis for textual_variant_involved=true. The genuinely solid datum is that Josh 21 and 1 Chr 6 are parallel divergent lists with a tribal-attribution discrepancy (Dan vs Ephraim) — that is a literary/source divergence, not by itself a manuscript variant. The claim of a relevant LXX variant at Josh 21:24 touching Aijalon's tribal assignment is not clearly substantiated and risks overstating the apparatus support. The BHS pointer at Josh 21:23-24 does not specifically resolve the Aijalon tribal-attribution question.
issues.correction: Either downgrade textual_variant_involved to false (treating this as a parallel-list/source divergence rather than a manuscript variant on the Aijalon attribution), or, if retained as true, restrict variant_description to the verified parallel-list divergence and avoid asserting a specific LXX Josh 21:24 variant unless it can be confirmed in the apparatus as bearing on Aijalon's tribe.

resolution.reasoning: The Dan-vs-Ephraim divergence is a parallel-list/source matter compounded by an internal scribal loss in the MT of Chronicles, not an attested manuscript variant on Aijalon's tribal attribution. 1 Chronicles 6:66-69 lists ten Kohathite cities but names only Ephraim and Manasseh as parent tribes; the tribe-of-Dan heading has dropped out of the Hebrew, so the Danite cities Aijalon and Gath-rimmon trail under the preceding Ephraim rubric. The standard restoration of 'out of the tribe of Dan' is a conjectural emendation drawn FROM Joshua 21 (Keil and Delitzsch, Ellicott, Barnes), with no manuscript witness preserving the Dan reading at this point, so most scholars, including critical ones, accept that the Ephraim labeling is a transmission artifact rather than an independent factual claim, which lands the call at probable_harmonization while still acknowledging the divergence is genuine in the received texts.
resolution.verification: Searched and read commentary aggregations and source-critical literature. BibleHub's collated commentaries on 1 Chronicles 6:69 confirm a lacuna: Ellicott ('Clearly there is a lacuna in our text between 1Chronicles 6:68-69'), Keil and Delitzsch ('a whole verse has been lost ... And of the tribe of Dan, Eltekeh ... cf. Joshua 21:23'), and Barnes ('something has fallen out ... We may supply from Joshua the words "out of Ephraim and out of Dan, and"') all explain the Ephraim attribution as a scribal omission of the Dan heading, restored by conjecture from Joshua 21 and NOT from any manuscript witness. The 'LXX of Joshua 21:24' variant the prior assessment leaned on could not be substantiated as bearing on Aijalon's tribal attribution: the actual LXX variation in this region concerns 'Elon-beth-hanan' in the Danite town list of Joshua 19:43-44 and the Aijalon/Elon vowel question, neither of which touches the Dan-vs-Ephraim Levitical-city assignment. Lee-Sak's JBL 136 (2017) study and the Tov material treat Josh 21 / 1 Chr 6 as parallel editions / source-list divergence, not as a single-point manuscript variant on Aijalon. On that evidence the textual-variant claim is withdrawn.
